title: The 48-hour rule
text: Wait two days before buying anything that is not a need. Most impulse urges fade on their own.

title: Track the small stuff
text: A $4 daily snack adds up to $120 a month. Write down every purchase for one month to see your real habits.

title: Pay yourself first
text: Move your savings amount aside the day your allowance arrives, before spending on anything else.

title: Audit your subscriptions
text: Check your subscriptions once a month and cancel anything you did not use in the last few weeks.

title: Weekly spending limit
text: Divide your monthly wants budget by four. A weekly number is much easier to stick to than a monthly one.

title: Buy used textbooks
text: Seniors, library copies and digital editions can cut book costs by half or more.

title: Name your savings goal
text: Saving for a 'laptop by March' feels more real than saving 'some money'. A name and date keep you motivated.

title: Start an emergency fund
text: Even $5 to $10 a month builds a buffer for surprises like a broken phone or a medical visit.

title: Use student discounts
text: Always ask if a student discount is available for transport, software, museums and food.

title: Cook in batches
text: Cooking a few meals at once with friends is cheaper than eating out and saves time during exams.

title: Review every month
text: Compare what you planned with what you actually spent. Adjust next month's plan, don't just feel guilty.

title: Round up and save
text: Round every purchase up to the nearest dollar in your tracker and move the difference into your goal each week.
